sections.overview: The Dusky Peacock is a geometrid moth recorded in Europe and North America.
sections.identification: It can resemble worn Macaria notata (Peacock Moth) or Macaria alternata (Sharp-angled Peacock), but lacks their dark-edged forewing notch.
sections.habitat: Its larvae use conifers; North American forest accounts list fir, spruce, hemlock, larch and related hosts.
sections.diet: In Canada, the form dispuncta feeds on many conifers, including Douglas-fir, western hemlock and Engelmann spruce.
sections.behavior: In Britain, adults fly after dark from May to July and are attracted to light.
sections.reproduction: The British account reports one generation per year and an established breeding population in Kent.
sections.ecology: Like Macaria liturata, it is a conifer-feeding moth; the documented host list for its North American form is broader than the Scots-pine emphasis for liturata.
sections.conservation: A French regional atlas labels it Near Threatened in Nouvelle-Aquitaine; that local status is not a global assessment.
